sections.h2: Choosing a route in New Berlin
sections.html:
A homeowner here can sign with an agent, handle the sale personally, or accept an offer from a cash buyer who wants the house without repairs. What tips the choice is usually the amount of work the property needs and the date you must be out. State rules covered below follow you down any of the three paths.

  • Agent listing. Exposure is widest, though buyers commonly ask for inspections and repair credits. The commission is set in your listing agreement, so see the percentage and every other charge on paper before you sign.
  • Private sale. Advertising, showings and the paperwork fall to you, the condition report and deed included.
  • Cash offer. Financing and repairs are normally off the table. Read the contract closely for the closing date, who pays for title work and any fee subtracted from your proceeds.

New Berlin lies in eastern Waukesha County, part of the Milwaukee metro area, and counts 39,953 residents. Owners occupy about 76.5 percent of homes, and 23.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Expect plenty of long-held houses with a string of renovations behind them. If yours is one, collect the permit history before a buyer asks for it.

The median owner-occupied value of $365,700 is a survey figure across all owner-occupied homes. Your own price will depend on condition, lot and timing instead.

sections.h2: School districts and your tax bill
sections.html:
No single district covers the city. Elmbrook, Muskego-Norway, New Berlin and West Allis-West Milwaukee all serve parts of it, and the city's Schools page lists them together with the private schools.

Tax rates change with the district a parcel falls in, as the city's Tax Levies and Rates page explains. Check the district named on your own tax bill first. Prospective buyers with children almost always open with that question.

Community Development, on the second floor of City Hall at 3805 S. Casper Drive, is the place to begin. Permit applications are accepted Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Inspectors cover the front counter from 8:00 to 9:00 am on weekdays, and reviewing a building permit may take up to 10 business days.

A buyer's inspector may compare the following kinds of past work with permit records.

  • New or replacement furnaces, air conditioners and water heaters
  • Decks, whether attached or detached, plus garages, sheds and similar accessory buildings
  • Kitchen remodels, additions, alterations and recreation rooms
  • Generators, hot tubs, pools and solar panels
  • Razing of a structure

If you cannot tell whether earlier work had a permit, phone Community Development before you list.

Water, sewer and stormwater bills also surface at closing. Wis. Stat. 66.0809 adds a 10 percent penalty to a utility balance still open after October 31, and a balance plus penalty can move onto the tax bill after November 15. Pay off anything outstanding before the sale. For the dates of the yearly notice, Open Book and Board of Review, ask the assessor's office.

Wis. Stat. 709.02 covers homes of one to four units. You complete a Real Estate Condition Report, and it must reach the buyer within 10 days of acceptance. When it comes late, the buyer holds two business days past the 10 to rescind and take the deposits back.

Think of the form as a disclosure and nothing more. It carries no warranty. Wis. Stat. 709.01 excuses court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived there, and it excuses transfers that escape the transfer fee. Learn something after you finish the report but before the buyer accepts, and Wis. Stat. 709.035 expects an amended report inside 10 days of acceptance. Answer every item. An unanswered line leaves the report incomplete in the statute's eyes.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts a state fee of 30 cents per $100 of value on the seller, collected by the register when the deed is submitted. Waukesha County asks you to round the price up to the next hundred before calculating. The Waukesha County Register of Deeds then charges $30 to record a deed.

Deed filing in Waukesha County
StepCost or ruleDetail
Transfer returnFiled electronicallyComplete the Real Estate Transfer Return on the Department of Revenue site and bring the receipt

Reach the recording office at 262-548-7585 or recording@waukeshacounty.gov. It is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Cash, credit and debit are all refused.

No fee applies to some transfers. Wis. Stat. 77.25 lists transfers by will, descent or survivorship, and a foreclosure deed or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder. After a spouse dies, the HT-110 form is the one to use, and the county asks for neither the tax bill nor a death certificate with it.

Before any buyer calls, assemble what a title company will want. That means the parcel number from your tax bill, your lender's payoff figure, permit records for earlier work and your school district. Add water, sewer and stormwater account information so the final bill closes out cleanly. If a deceased spouse is still on the title, plan on the HT-110 form, a transfer return receipt and a copy of the document that shows the interest.

Then make each buyer or agent put the same answers in writing: the closing date, the fees deducted from your proceeds and what happens if an inspection finds a problem. Offers become easy to compare once they carry the same facts.

faqs.q: Is an as-is sale possible in New Berlin?
faqs.a: Yes. You can ask for an as-is sale in the contract, and many cash buyers work that way. The condition report is a separate duty, so unless you are exempt you still give the buyer a finished report within 10 days of acceptance.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee when a New Berlin home sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor at 30 cents per $100 of value, and the register collects it at recording. Agree in the contract on who covers other closing charges.

faqs.q: How fast does Waukesha County return a recorded deed?
faqs.a: An e-recorded deed comes back at once. For paper, supply a valid email address and the document is returned right after recording, or enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope and wait two to three weeks.

faqs.q: What do I file when a co-owner has died?
faqs.a: Form HT-110, the Termination of Decedent's Interest, with a transfer return receipt, a copy of the document showing the decedent's interest and a $30 check or money order. Confirm details with the office or an attorney.

faqs.q: Do unpaid utility bills affect a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Any balance still open after October 31 takes a 10 percent penalty, and the balance plus penalty may land on the tax bill after November 15. Clear water, sewer and stormwater charges before closing.
